title: Okra Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Okra Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Okra nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and phosphorus in okra, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Okra nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your okra turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, zinc, boron, magnesium and calcium. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Nitrogen deficiency on a leaf, shown on another crop as a stand in for okra
heroImage.credit: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But zinc, boron and calcium stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which okra nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.
Okra nutrient deficiency signs, old leaves and young leaves
Shows first on the old leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the old leaves of okra

Muriate of potash 0 0 60, Sulfate of potash 0 0 50

blocks.text: Shows first on the young leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the young leaves of okra
rows: young leaves and the tip, between the veins
Young leaves yellow between the veins, turn whitish and stay few and small.
young leaves and the tip, fruit, grain or tubers
New leaves are small and brittle, and pods stay short and misshapen with few seeds.
young leaves and the tip, the roots
Growing tips brown and die, and young leaves rosette with ragged, upturned edges.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a okra nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest okra nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in okra

Older leaves turn pale to light green, then die or drop. Plants are stunted with small leaves and thin shoots, and pods are pale, small, thick or misshapen, so yield falls. You see it most at this stage: vegetative growth and the picking period.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in okra
Sandy soils, heavy rain, low organic matter, and no side dressing once picking starts.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium shortage yellows the middle of mature leaves while the edges stay green. Yellow vein mosaic virus turns the veins yellow in a net pattern. To be sure, old leaves yellow first. Soil test and leaf tissue test.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency
Side dress urea based on the soil test. For a quick fix, KAU gives a urea leaf spray at 10 grams per liter of water every 15 days.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, add manure at planting and side dress during the picking season.
Potassium deficiency in okra

Older leaves yellow and scorch and then drop, with yellowing along the edges while the leaf base stays dark green. The plant carries fewer leaves. You see it most at this stage: flowering and picking.
Why potassium deficiency happens in okra
Sandy or acid soils (potassium is readily available only above about pH 6), heavy rain, and urea only feeding.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium shortage yellows the middle of the leaf instead of the edges. To be sure, soil test for potassium and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply muriate of potash based on the soil test, in split doses. For an immediate remedy, KAU gives a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water with a sticker. Lime or dolomite on acid soil and wood ash help.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include potash at planting and during picking.
Phosphorus deficiency in okra

Older leaves look greener than normal and then turn purple. Plants have fewer leaves, short thin shoots, weak roots and poor pods, and growth is stunted. You see it most at this stage: seedling and early growth.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in okra
Acid or iron rich soils, low organic matter, and no phosphorus at planting. Phosphorus is best taken up near pH 6.2 to 7.0.
How to tell it apart
Root knot nematodes also stunt okra. Check roots for galls. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency
Apply the recommended phosphorus fertilizer on schedule based on the soil test. KAU lists single superphosphate for a quick correction and bone meal or rock phosphate for the long term.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use complete fertilizer or 16 20 0 at planting and lime very acid soil.
Zinc deficiency in okra
Young leaves yellow between the veins and can turn white. Leaf size and number drop, leaves look mottled and stems are thin. You see it most at this stage: vegetative growth.
Why zinc deficiency happens in okra
High pH or overlimed soils, heavy phosphorus, and waterlogged soils. Zinc is best available at pH 5 to 7.5.
How to tell it apart
Yellow vein mosaic virus makes the veins themselves yellow. Zinc shortage keeps veins green. To be sure, soil test for zinc and pH, and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

KAU suggests zinc sulfate in the soil at about 20 kg per hectare (8 kg per acre). In severe cases a morning spray of zinc sulfate at 2 grams plus calcium carbonate at 2.5 grams per liter of water. Do not apply zinc and phosphate together.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep pH in the 5 to 7.5 range and avoid excess phosphorus.
Boron deficiency in okra

Young leaves are malformed, small and brittle, and growth is stunted. Pods are small and misshapen with poor seed set, and some stay as short stumps. You see it most at this stage: flowering and pod set.
Why boron deficiency happens in okra
Sandy soils, overlimed soils, low organic matter and drought.
How to tell it apart
Pod deformity also comes from insect feeding (fruit borer, sucking bugs). Check for holes and insects. To be sure, soil test for boron and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for boron deficiency

KAU suggests borax in the soil at about 10 kg per hectare (4 kg per acre), or a borax spray at 1 gram per liter of water. Delaware lists okra among crops with a medium boron need, about 2 pounds of boron per acre before planting. Do not mix borax with calcium or ammonium fertilizer.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add a small boron dose to the basal fertilizer on sandy soils.
Magnesium deficiency in okra

Fully expanded leaves show it first: the middle of the blade yellows while the edges stay green. Leaves may drop early or show spotted dead patches, and yield drops. You see it most at this stage: flowering and picking.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in okra
Acid sandy soils and heavy potash fertilizer.
How to tell it apart
Potassium shortage scorches the edges instead. To be sure, soil test for magnesium and potassium.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency
KAU suggests magnesium sulfate in a band near the plants at about 80 kg per hectare (32 kg per acre). Do not apply magnesium and potassium fertilizer together.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, long term use of dolomite on acid soil.
Calcium deficiency in okra

Young leaves are hit first. Root and shoot tips brown and die, internodes shorten so leaves form rosettes, leaf edges become ragged and brittle and curl upward, and pod quality drops. You see it most at this stage: vegetative growth and early flowering.
Why calcium deficiency happens in okra
Very acid soils, excess phosphorus, and boron shortage, which can also bring on calcium shortage.
How to tell it apart
Boron shortage also damages young growth. Check both with a soil test. To be sure, soil test for calcium, pH and boron.
What to apply for calcium deficiency
KAU suggests lime at about 250 kg per hectare when soil pH is 5.5 to 6, or about 840 kg per hectare in two doses when pH is 3.5 to 4.5. Gypsum on soil that is not acid.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soil before planting.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any okra nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your okra needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Okra nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my okra leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: lower leaves pale and drop, and pods come small, pale and misshapen. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in okra?
items.a: Side dress urea based on the soil test. For a quick fix, KAU gives a urea leaf spray at 10 grams per liter of water every 15 days.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in okra?
items.a: Apply muriate of potash based on the soil test, in split doses. For an immediate remedy, KAU gives a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water with a sticker.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in okra?
items.a: Apply the recommended phosphorus fertilizer on schedule based on the soil test. KAU lists single superphosphate for a quick correction and bone meal or rock phosphate for the long term.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my okra lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the okra nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
